_comment: KPI gates for the Open5GS stack. Same schema and the same gate tool as the free5GC set
(deployments/kpi-gates.json); run with `make o5gs-gate`.
Every metric below was checked against ground truth on the running stack (20 UE interfaces,
10 per slice) before being trusted. Deliberately NOT used, because they read wrong:
fivegs_smffunction_sm_qos_flow_nbr        read 20/20 against 10/10 real flows — never
decremented when UEs re-attach
fivegs_smffunction_sm_pdusessioncreationsucc  read 40 per slice for 20 requests — counts
each success twice (a 200% success ratio)
fivegs_smffunction_sm_pdusessioncreationreq   also emits an unlabelled duplicate series,
so a plain sum() double-counts
The one exact per-slice count is sm_sessionnbr (SMF, by S-NSSAI).
fivegs_upffunction_upf_sessionnbr / upf_qosflows  correct at first, then 21 sessions and 11 flows
for 20/10 real after ONE UE restart — lower bounds only
Unlike the free5GC set, the user-plane gates here are runnable: the Open5GS UPF needs no
kernel module (ADR-010).
Core-side metrics cannot see UEs that disappear: with all 20 UEs stopped, every gate above
the UE-reachability ones still passed. Liveness and latency come from ue_probe_exporter.
Phase 2b (ADR-014): three slices and 100 UEs — eMBB 20, URLLC 10, mMTC 70. Counts are per
slice at each slice's own size (O5GS_UES in deployments/slices.env). These are DEPLOYMENT
gates — is every slice up and serving its UEs. The per-slice service KPIs compared against
industry targets belong to the Phase 2b KPI scorecard, which Track 3 owns.

gates.title: All 6 Open5GS metric exporters are scrapeable
gates.why: AMF, SMF, PCF and the three per-slice UPFs are the NFs that export metrics; losing one blinds the gate to that part of the network.

gates.title: No network or exporter target is down
gates.why: Includes the per-slice traffic and UE probe exporters: a broken observability plane must fail the gate rather than report a silent green. The slice orchestrator is excluded — it is an optional host process above the network, and a stopped orchestrator once failed this gate on a healthy stack; it has its own advisory.

gates.title: The SMF is associated over N4 with all three slice UPFs
gates.why: One UPF per slice (ADR-011). Without a PFCP association the SMF cannot install forwarding rules for that slice, and its sessions carry nothing even if they are accepted.

gates.title: All three slice gNBs are connected over N2
gates.why: One gNB per slice (ADR-011). A missing gNB means an entire slice has no radio access, while the other slices keep every KPI green.

gates.title: All 100 UEs are attached
gates.why: Matched the UE interfaces exactly in the ground-truth audit (20 UEs, then 100), unlike free5GC's AMF gauges.

gates.title: Every UE has a user-plane session at the UPF
gates.why: Counted where traffic is carried, not where it is signalled: a session the UPF does not hold cannot forward a packet (ODE-only on free5GC). A LOWER bound only: after one UE was restarted the UPF reported 21 sessions for 20 real ones while the SMF correctly reported 20, so this gauge can over-count and must never be used as an exact total.

gates.title: Each slice's own UPF holds sessions
gates.why: With a UPF per slice, the UPF's native session gauge becomes per-slice. Presence only: the gauge over-counts after UE restarts, so it is never used as an exact count.

gates.title: eMBB holds its 20 PDU sessions
gates.why: The SMF's session gauge is labelled by S-NSSAI and was exact in every audit. One gate per slice at that slice's own size (O5GS_UES in slices.env): with slices of 20, 10 and 70, a min() across them could only ever check the smallest. `or vector(0)`: a slice with no series at all must fail, not vanish.

gates.title: URLLC holds its 10 PDU sessions
gates.why: The SMF's session gauge is labelled by S-NSSAI and was exact in every audit. One gate per slice at that slice's own size (O5GS_UES in slices.env): with slices of 20, 10 and 70, a min() across them could only ever check the smallest. `or vector(0)`: a slice with no series at all must fail, not vanish.

gates.title: mMTC holds its 70 PDU sessions
gates.why: The SMF's session gauge is labelled by S-NSSAI and was exact in every audit. One gate per slice at that slice's own size (O5GS_UES in slices.env): with slices of 20, 10 and 70, a min() across them could only ever check the smallest. `or vector(0)`: a slice with no series at all must fail, not vanish.

gates.title: All three slices appear in the SMF's slice-labelled metrics
gates.why: Guards the per-slice session gates against a slice vanishing from the metrics entirely.

gates.title: The UPFs hold QoS flows for all three slices' DNNs
gates.why: Each slice has its own DNN (internet = eMBB, urllc = URLLC, iot = mMTC), so this confirms slice separation inside the user plane. Counts presence per DNN only: after a UE restart the UPF reported 11 flows on 'internet' for 10 real sessions.

gates.title: All three slices' UPF devices are measurable
gates.why: Native UPF volume counters are labelled only by QFI and cannot separate slices; per-slice throughput depends entirely on this exporter.

gates.title: Every eMBB UE (20) answered through its UPF within 30 s
gates.why: The only liveness signal measured from the UE side: with every UE stopped, the AMF still reported every UE and the UPF every session. Windowed over 30 s because one probe lost in a single 5 s round is not a dead UE; a UE that is really gone never answers, and the UE supervisor restarts it within ~30 s. One gate per slice at its own size.

gates.title: Every URLLC UE (10) answered through its UPF within 30 s
gates.why: The only liveness signal measured from the UE side: with every UE stopped, the AMF still reported every UE and the UPF every session. Windowed over 30 s because one probe lost in a single 5 s round is not a dead UE; a UE that is really gone never answers, and the UE supervisor restarts it within ~30 s. One gate per slice at its own size.

gates.title: Every mMTC UE (70) answered through its UPF within 30 s
gates.why: The only liveness signal measured from the UE side: with every UE stopped, the AMF still reported every UE and the UPF every session. Windowed over 30 s because one probe lost in a single 5 s round is not a dead UE; a UE that is really gone never answers, and the UE supervisor restarts it within ~30 s. One gate per slice at its own size.

gates.title: URLLC average round-trip time within its 10 ms budget (1 min)
gates.why: SLICE_B_MAX_LATENCY_MS in slices.env, measured UE -> gNB -> UPF on the slice's own path. Enforced on the average: measured 2.9-3.4 ms idle and under eMBB load. The worst case is reported separately as advisory because it already exceeds 10 ms at idle on this host.

gates.title: eMBB worst round-trip time within its 300 ms budget (1 min)
gates.why: SLICE_A_MAX_LATENCY_MS in slices.env, measured the same way as URLLC.

gates.title: mMTC worst round-trip time within its 1000 ms budget (1 min)
gates.why: SLICE_C_MAX_LATENCY_MS in slices.env: an IoT report may take up to a second. Measured the same way as the other slices. The slice's own KPIs (device density, delivery of small reports) belong to the Phase 2b KPI scorecard, not to this deployment gate.

gates.title: URLLC worst-case round-trip time within 10 ms (1 min)
gates.why: Advisory, and expected to WARN on this laptop: the worst probe of a minute measured 10.14 and 10.95 ms at IDLE in two runs. A software UPF and simulated RAN sharing a laptop CPU cannot hold a URLLC tail budget; this states that plainly instead of hiding it behind an average.

gates.title: No URLLC probe lost in the last minute
gates.why: Advisory: the slice-isolation signal. With eMBB saturated at 350-470 Mbps, URLLC lost up to 4 of 10 probes per round (idle: none) while its average RTT did not change — the slices share fate through packet loss, not delay.

gates.title: No UE registration failures in the last 5 minutes
gates.why: Advisory: failures are expected for a few minutes after the Docker engine restarts underneath running UEs, which recover on retry.

gates.title: All three slices carried user traffic in the last 5 minutes
gates.why: Advisory: an idle network is not a broken one. Reported so that a demo or test run shows traffic genuinely reached every slice. The UE probes alone keep this true while the UEs are up.

gates.title: The slice orchestrator is being scraped
gates.why: Advisory: demand admission is unavailable while it is down, but the network itself is unaffected. Start it with scripts/open5gs/start_orchestrator.sh.
